title: Nutritional Sciences, B.S. — Nutrition and Dietetics Option (College of Health and Human Development)
notes:
Nutrition and Dietetics Option, University Park (of two; the Health Sciences option relies heavily on 'Any NUTR course' / 'Any NUTR 400-level course' placeholders with no anchor structure, whereas Dietetics has concrete required courses throughout). Added a new hm_catalog.json for HM 230/330 (Hospitality Management department, needed for the food-service-management requirement). Chose 'CHEM 202' over 'CHEM 210' since CHEM 202's prereq (CHEM 110) is directly satisfied by this plan, while CHEM 210 needs CHEM 112, not otherwise scheduled. Explicitly scheduled ENGL 15 (Semester 1), ENGL 202C (Semester 5), and CAS 100A (Semester 8) rather than generic 'GWS course' slots, since NUTR 445/446/451/452 and other downstream courses depend on specific prereq chains that a generic domain-slot pick isn't guaranteed to satisfy. 'NUTR 495' (Advanced Field Experience, listed as a Summer course) is scheduled as a regular-term item since the engine paces by credit cap, not literal summer/fall/spring labels. 'Supporting 400-level course' and generic 'University-Wide Offering' pools are modeled generically, same convention as CMPSC's own open pools. Post-parens-fix re-scrape (AND/OR prereq-parsing bug fix) revealed CHEM 110/CHEM 130 and STAT 200/STAT 250 all real-require MATH 21 (CHEM 110 via MATH 22, which itself needs MATH 21), which itself real-chains through MATH 4 and MATH 3 -- none of these were in the plan (MATH wasn't even in departments), permanently blocking the CHEM/STAT items. Added MATH to departments and the real chain explicitly: MATH 3 (Semester 1), MATH 4 (Semester 2), MATH 21 (Semester 3) -- same convention used for LSCPE/ABSM/ACCTG's identical gap. The added 9cr didn't fit in 8 terms at the original 17cr/semester cap -- bumped max_credits_per_semester to 18, matching the pattern used elsewhere this session for the same MATH-chain gap. Handbook verification pass: cross-checked against the live bulletin (bulletins.psu.edu, 2026-27 edition) and the department's own real, live Supporting Course List page (hhd.psu.edu/nutrition/supporting-courses) -- this major is ACEND-accredited (Didactic Program in Dietetics), so its prescribed-course list is unusually fixed; every required course in this plan (BMB 211, CHEM 111, HM 230, HM 330, MICRB 106, NUTR 320/358/360/361/386/391/393/400/445/446/453/495, plus the common BIOL 161-164/NUTR 251/451/452/490W and STAT 200/250) already matches the live bulletin's Nutrition and Dietetics option exactly -- no drift found. The 3 generic 'Supporting Course (400-level)' slots (9cr total) and 2 generic 'University-Wide Offering' slots (6cr total) exactly match the bulletin's own 'Select 9 credits of 400-level supporting courses' and 'Select 6 credits from university-wide offerings' requirements -- wired both to the department's real Supporting Course List. Per that page's own restriction text ('Any NUTR course numbered 101 or higher not required to meet the major degree requirements can be a supporting course... an exception is NUTR 119... NUTR 100 (3 cr) cannot be used') this plan does not add NUTR 100/119 to either options list. A handful of the real list's codes (FOR 201, GEOG 123, HDFS 210Z, SOC 210Z, SOC 211Z, SPAN 100C, WMNST 452, AGBM 170Z) have no matching entry in this app's own scraped catalogs (a scraping gap) -- left in as unchecked fallback options. AMST, INTAG, RSOC, and AG (generic) have no catalog file for their department at all in this app -- their few listed codes (AMST 106N, INTAG 100N, RSOC 11, AG 400) are likewise left in as unchecked literal fallbacks rather than fabricated or dropped.

2026 vs 2023 historical-year check: fetched the real archived 2023-24 bulletin edition, raw HTML, cross-checked against its own printed credit subtotals (its Nutrition and Dietetics Option is printed as '(64 credits)', and Common Requirements for the Major (All Options) + Option combined sums to the page's own stated 'Requirements for the Major 88-91' range once STAT 200/250's 3-4cr range and the other two options' wider ranges are accounted for). Real, verified differences from 2026-27, all fixed in this file: (1) CHEM 111 (1cr) was not required at all that year -- not in the Program Requirements course list, not on the Suggested Academic Plan -- removed from this file's schedule. (2) MICRB 107 (Elementary Microbiology Laboratory, 1cr) WAS a required prescribed course, always paired with MICRB 106 (the suggested plan lists them jointly as 'MICRB 106 & MICRB 107 (GN)') -- added back into this file's Semester 3, right after MICRB 106 (its real concurrent-group prereq in this app's own micrb_catalog.json is exactly ['MICRB 106'], so same-term placement is prereq-safe). (3) NUTR 211R (Applying Biochemistry to Nutrition, 1cr) WAS also a required prescribed course that year (dropped from the Nutrition and Dietetics option entirely by 2024-25) -- added into this file's Semester 5; its real prereq_groups in this app's own nutr_catalog.json require CHEM 202/210/210H AND BMB 211 both completed (not concurrent), both of which are scheduled earlier in this same flowchart (Semester 3 and Semester 4), so Semester 5 keeps it prereq-safe. (4) NUTR 400 was 2 credits that year (same as 2024-25; only became 3cr in 2025-26) -- fixed in this file's Semester 7. (5) The Supporting Courses requirement that year was a single 'Select 9 credits ... at least 6 credits must be at the 400 level, no more than 3 may be NUTR 496' pool, not the 6cr-university-wide-at-any-level + 9cr-400-level 15-credit split that first appears in the 2024-25 edition -- this file drops one 'University-Wide Offering' (3cr) item and one 'Supporting Course (400-level)' (3cr) item, leaving 3cr university-wide + 6cr 400-level = 9cr total, satisfying the real 'at least 6cr at 400-level' rule for that year's smaller pool. Everything else in the combined Common + Option course list (BIOL 161/162/163/164, BMB 211, CHEM 110/130, CHEM 202/210, HDFS 129/PSYCH 100, HM 230, HM 330, MICRB 106, NUTR 251/320/358/360/361/386/391/393/445/446/451/452/453/490W/495, STAT 200/250) already matches 2026-27 exactly that year -- confirmed by direct comparison of both years' printed Program Requirements course lists.
